native_statement.reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega be any measurable space and let mu be any measure on Omega. Let H=L^2(mu;R), the real Hilbert space of almost-everywhere equivalence classes of measurable square-integrable real functions. For any bounded continuous real-linear operators A,B:H->H, if A and B are positive (symmetric with nonnegative quadratic forms) and A composed with A equals B composed with B as operators, then A=B as operators.
native_statement.objects: Caller-supplied objects are the measurable space Omega, measure mu and operators A and B. No operator or root is constructed existentially. Multiplication A*A and B*B means operator composition. Positivity means symmetry together with <Au,u> >= 0 for all u, and correspondingly for B; on this complete real Hilbert space this gives selfadjointness.
native_statement.domains: Omega is an arbitrary type with a measurable-space structure. mu is an arbitrary measure: neither probability, finiteness nor sigma-finiteness is an explicit assumption. H is complete and may be zero-dimensional or infinite-dimensional; it is not asserted to be finite-dimensional.
native_statement.quantifiers: Universally quantify Omega, its measurable-space structure, mu, A and B. Under the three caller hypotheses A positive, B positive and equality of their squares, conclude A=B. There is no existential object and no quantification over energy certificates.
assumptions: A is a bounded continuous real-linear operator on H
B is a bounded continuous real-linear operator on H
native_statement.conclusion: Equality A=B of the bounded operators on the same H, so they act identically on every L2 equivalence class.
native_statement.scopes: The square equality is a caller premise, not a produced certificate. The result is uniqueness among positive bounded operators with a common square. It neither constructs a square root for an arbitrary operator nor supplies a separate energy identity. It does not assert uniqueness among roots without positivity.
native_statement.constant_dependencies: There are no numerical constants, asymptotic estimates, dimension caps or hidden energy/root hypotheses.
nonclaims: No existence of a positive square root for arbitrary input operators
No uniqueness for nonsymmetric or nonpositive alternatives
No CFC, extension or energy premise or conclusion
